fields.text: EEPROM address, linear across the 512, 1K, 2K or 4K byte EEPROM (0 up to 511, 1023, 2047 or 4096). EEARH and EEARL together hold it; its reset value is undefined, so it must be written with a valid address before any EEPROM access.

fields.name: EEAR
fields.text: EEPROM address, linear across the 512, 1K, 2K or 4K byte EEPROM (0 up to 511, 1023, 2047 or 4096). EEARH and EEARL together hold it; its reset value is undefined, so it must be written with a valid address before any EEPROM access.

fields.name: EEDR
fields.text: EEPROM data: on a write, the byte to store at the EEAR address; on a read, the byte read back from the EEAR address.

fields.name: EEPM
fields.text: EEPROM programming mode: picks what a write of EEPE does, either erase and write together in one atomic step or erase and write as two separate operations. Writes to EEPM are ignored while EEPE is 1. Reset sets EEPM to 0b00 unless the EEPROM is busy programming. Settings: 0b00 erase and write in one atomic operation, 3.4 ms; 0b01 erase only, 1.8 ms; 0b10 write only, 1.8 ms; 0b11 reserved.

rows: Erase and write together, one atomic operation.

fields.name: EERIE
fields.text: EEPROM ready interrupt enable: 1 enables the EEPROM Ready interrupt when SREG.I is 1, 0 disables it. The interrupt keeps firing for as long as EEPE is 0.

fields.name: EEMPE
fields.text: EEPROM master programming enable: while EEMPE is 1, setting EEPE within four clock cycles writes the EEPROM at the selected address; while it is 0, setting EEPE does nothing. Hardware clears EEMPE four clock cycles after software sets it.

fields.name: EEPE
fields.text: EEPROM programming enable, the write strobe: with address and data set up and EEMPE written to 1 first, writing EEPE to 1 starts the write; without EEMPE no write happens. Write sequence: wait for EEPE to read 0; wait for SPMCSR.SPMEN to read 0; load EEAR and EEDR if needed (either order); write EEMPE to 1 while writing EEPE to 0; within four clock cycles write EEPE to 1. The EEPROM cannot be written while the CPU writes Flash; the SPMEN wait matters only when a boot loader writes Flash. An interrupt between the last two steps makes the write fail as EEMPE times out, and an interrupt routine that touches EEAR or EEDR during an access makes that access fail; keeping SREG.I cleared through the steps avoids both. Hardware clears EEPE when the write time has passed. Setting EEPE halts the CPU for two cycles before the next instruction.

fields.name: EERE
fields.text: EEPROM read enable, the read strobe: with the address in EEAR, writing EERE to 1 starts the read, which completes in one instruction with the data ready at once; the CPU halts four cycles before the next instruction. EEPE is polled before a read: while a write is in progress the EEPROM cannot be read nor EEAR changed. Access timing comes from the calibrated oscillator.

fields.name: CAL
fields.text: Oscillator calibration: trims the calibrated internal RC oscillator for process variation. Reset loads a factory value giving the factory calibrated frequency; software may write other values to change the frequency, and calibration outside the specified range is not guaranteed. The oscillator also times EEPROM and Flash writes, so their times move with it; calibrating above 8.8 MHz while writing EEPROM or Flash can make the write fail. CAL7 selects the range, 0 the lower and 1 the higher; the two ranges overlap, so 0x7F is faster than 0x80. CAL6:0 tune within the range, 0x00 slowest and 0x7F fastest.

fields.name: JTRF
fields.text: JTAG reset flag: set by a reset coming from a 1 in the JTAG Reset Register, which the AVR_RESET instruction selects. A power-on reset or a write of 0 clears it.

fields.name: WDRF
fields.text: Watchdog reset flag: set by a watchdog reset. Cleared by writing 0 or by a power-on reset.

fields.name: BORF
fields.text: Brown-out reset flag: set by a brown-out reset. Cleared by writing 0 or by a power-on reset.

fields.name: EXTRF
fields.text: External reset flag: set by an external reset. Cleared by writing 0 or by a power-on reset.

fields.name: PORF
fields.text: Power-on reset flag: set by a power-on reset; cleared only by writing 0. Reading MCUSR and then clearing it early in the program lets the flags show the source of the next reset.

fields.name: WDIF
fields.text: Watchdog interrupt flag: set on a watchdog time-out when the watchdog is configured for interrupt. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. The time-out interrupt runs when SREG.I and WDIE are both 1.

fields.name: WDIE
fields.text: Watchdog interrupt enable: with WDIE at 1 and SREG.I at 1 the watchdog interrupt is enabled. With WDE at 0 the watchdog is in Interrupt Mode and a time-out runs the interrupt; with WDE at 1 the mode is Interrupt and System Reset: a first time-out sets WDIF, running the vector clears WDIE and WDIF in hardware and leaves the watchdog in System Reset Mode, and a time-out before the interrupt runs resets the system. Staying in Interrupt and System Reset Mode takes setting WDIE again after each interrupt, not from inside the interrupt routine.

rows: Interrupt first, then System Reset Mode.

fields.name: WDP3
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 3: with WDP2:0, sets the watchdog prescaling and so its time-out period while it runs. WDP3:0 settings, in WDT oscillator cycles with the typical time-out at VCC = 5.0 V: 0b0000 2K, 16 ms; 0b0001 4K, 32 ms; 0b0010 8K, 64 ms; 0b0011 16K, 0.125 s; 0b0100 32K, 0.25 s; 0b0101 64K, 0.5 s; 0b0110 128K, 1.0 s; 0b0111 256K, 2.0 s; 0b1000 512K, 4.0 s; 0b1001 1024K, 8.0 s; 0b1010 to 0b1111 reserved.

fields.name: WDCE
fields.text: Watchdog change enable: must be 1 to clear WDE or change the prescaler bits, in a timed sequence. Hardware clears it four clock cycles after it is written to 1.

fields.name: WDE
fields.text: Watchdog system reset enable: forced to 1 while MCUSR.WDRF is 1, so WDRF must be cleared before WDE can be. This keeps repeated resets coming under failure conditions and gives a safe start-up afterwards.

fields.name: WDP2
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 2: with the other WDP3:0 bits, sets the watchdog prescaling and so its time-out period while it runs.

fields.name: WDP0

fields.name: IVSEL
fields.text: Interrupt vector select: 0 puts the interrupt vectors at the start of Flash, 1 moves them to the start of the boot loader section, whose address the BOOTSZ fuses set. Changing IVSEL takes a timed sequence: write IVCE to 1, then within four cycles write the new IVSEL value with IVCE at 0. Interrupts are off from the cycle IVCE is set until after the instruction following the IVSEL write, or for four cycles if IVSEL is not written; SREG.I is not changed by this. When BLB02 is programmed and the vectors sit in the boot loader section, interrupts are off while code runs from the application section; when BLB12 is programmed and the vectors sit in the application section, interrupts are off while code runs from the boot loader section.

fields.name: IVCE
fields.text: Interrupt vector change enable: must be written to 1 before IVSEL can change. Hardware clears it four cycles after the write, or when IVSEL is written. Setting IVCE disables interrupts.

fields.name: ISC2
fields.text: External interrupt 2 sense control: picks the level or edge on INT2 that triggers the interrupt, which runs when SREG.I and the matching EIMSK bit are 1. Edges on INT2:0 are detected asynchronously; pulses wider than the minimum pulse width always interrupt, shorter ones may not. A low-level trigger must hold until the current instruction completes, and keeps requesting for as long as the pin stays low. Changing ISCn can itself raise an interrupt, so the INTn enable in EIMSK is cleared first, ISCn changed, then INTFn in EIFR cleared by writing 1 before re-enabling.

Writing 1 forces an immediate compare match on the waveform generator, changing OC2A as COM2A1:0 dictate at that moment. It is a strobe: it raises no interrupt, does not clear the timer in CTC mode with OCR2A as TOP, and always reads 0.

It is a strobe: it raises no interrupt, does not clear the timer in CTC mode with OCR2B as TOP, and always reads 0.

fields.name: EXCLK
fields.text: Enable external clock input: with EXCLK at 1 and the asynchronous clock selected, the TOSC1 input buffer takes an external clock in place of a 32 kHz crystal. EXCLK is written before asynchronous operation is selected. The crystal oscillator runs only while EXCLK is 0.

fields.name: AS2
fields.text: Asynchronous Timer/Counter2: 0 clocks Timer/Counter2 from clkI/O, 1 from a crystal oscillator on TOSC1. Changing AS2 may corrupt TCNT2, OCR2A, OCR2B, TCCR2A and TCCR2B.

fields.name: TCN2UB
fields.text: Timer/Counter2 update busy: in asynchronous operation, set when TCNT2 is written and cleared by hardware once TCNT2 has taken the value from its temporary register. 0 means TCNT2 is ready for a new value.

fields.name: OCR2AUB
fields.text: Output compare register 2 A update busy: in asynchronous operation, set when OCR2A is written and cleared by hardware once OCR2A has taken the value from its temporary register. 0 means OCR2A is ready for a new value.

fields.name: OCR2BUB
fields.text: Output compare register 2 B update busy: in asynchronous operation, set when OCR2B is written and cleared by hardware once OCR2B has taken the value from its temporary register. 0 means OCR2B is ready for a new value.

fields.name: TCR2AUB
fields.text: Timer/counter control register 2 A update busy: in asynchronous operation, set when TCCR2A is written and cleared by hardware once TCCR2A has taken the value from its temporary register. 0 means TCCR2A is ready for a new value.

fields.name: TCR2BUB
fields.text: Timer/counter control register 2 B update busy: in asynchronous operation, set when TCCR2B is written and cleared by hardware once TCCR2B has taken the value from its temporary register. 0 means TCCR2B is ready for a new value. A write to one of these five Timer/Counter2 registers while its own busy flag is 1 can corrupt the value and cause an unintended interrupt. Reading TCNT2 returns the actual count; reading OCR2A, OCR2B, TCCR2A or TCCR2B returns the temporary register.

fields.name: OCIE2B
fields.text: Timer/Counter2 output compare match B interrupt enable: with OCIE2B and SREG.I at 1, the interrupt runs on a compare match, when TIFR2.OCF2B is set.

fields.name: OCIE2A
fields.text: Timer/Counter2 output compare match A interrupt enable: with OCIE2A and SREG.I at 1, the interrupt runs on a compare match, when TIFR2.OCF2A is set.

fields.name: TOIE2
fields.text: Timer/Counter2 overflow interrupt enable: with TOIE2 and SREG.I at 1, the interrupt runs on an overflow, when TIFR2.TOV2 is set.

fields.name: OCF2B
fields.text: Output compare flag 2 B: set when Timer/Counter2 matches OCR2B. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. The interrupt runs when SREG.I, OCIE2B and OCF2B are all 1.

fields.name: OCF2A
fields.text: Output compare flag 2 A: set when Timer/Counter2 matches OCR2A. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. The interrupt runs when SREG.I, OCIE2A and OCF2A are all 1.

fields.name: TOV2
fields.text: Timer/Counter2 overflow flag: set when Timer/Counter2 overflows; in PWM mode, set when the counter turns around at 0x00. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. The interrupt runs when SREG.I, TOIE2 and TOV2 are all 1.

fields.name: TSM
fields.text: Timer/Counter synchronization mode: 1 holds whatever is written to PSRASY and PSRSYNC, keeping those prescalers in reset so their timers stay halted and can be set up alike without one advancing. Writing TSM to 0 makes hardware clear PSRASY and PSRSYNC, and the timers start counting together.

fields.name: PSRASY
fields.text: Prescaler reset Timer/Counter2: 1 resets the Timer/Counter2 prescaler. Hardware normally clears it at once; in asynchronous mode it stays 1 until the reset is done, and while TSM is 1 hardware does not clear it.

fields.name: PSRSYNC
fields.text: Prescaler reset: 1 resets the prescaler shared by Timer/Counter1 and Timer/Counter0, affecting both. Hardware normally clears it at once, except while TSM is 1.

registers.name: SPCR
registers.title: SPI Control Register
notes: The register summary prints bit 7 as SPIE0, bit 6 as SPE0, bit 5 as DORD0, bit 4 as MSTR0, bit 3 as CPOL0, bit 2 as CPHA0, bit 1 as SPR01, bit 0 as SPR00.

fields.name: SPIE
fields.text: SPI interrupt enable: with SPIE at 1, the SPI interrupt runs when SPSR.SPIF and SREG.I are both 1.

fields.name: SPE
fields.text: SPI enable: must be 1 for any SPI operation.

fields.name: DORD
fields.text: Data order: 1 sends the data word LSB first, 0 MSB first.

fields.name: MSTR
fields.text: Master/slave select: 1 selects master, 0 slave. Pulling an SS input low while MSTR is 1 clears MSTR and sets SPSR.SPIF; software then sets MSTR again to return to master.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: Clock polarity: 1 holds SCK high when idle, 0 low. With 0 the leading edge rises and the trailing edge falls; with 1 the leading edge falls and the trailing edge rises.

fields.name: CPHA
fields.text: Clock phase: picks the SCK edge data is sampled on. 0 samples on the leading edge and sets up on the trailing edge; 1 sets up on the leading edge and samples on the trailing edge.

fields.name: SPR
fields.text: SPI clock rate select: with SPSR.SPI2X, sets SCK in master mode as a fraction of fosc; no effect in slave mode. With SPI2X at 0: 0b00 fosc/4, 0b01 fosc/16, 0b10 fosc/64, 0b11 fosc/128. With SPI2X at 1: 0b00 fosc/2, 0b01 fosc/8, 0b10 fosc/32, 0b11 fosc/64.

registers.name: SPSR
registers.title: SPI Status Register
notes: The settings of SPI2X are carried on SPCR.SPR, which holds the low bits.
The register summary prints bit 7 as SPIF0, bit 6 as WCOL0, bit 0 as SPI2X0.

fields.name: SPIF
fields.text: SPI interrupt flag: set when a serial transfer completes, and also when SS is an input driven low in master mode; raises an interrupt when SPCR.SPIE and global interrupts are enabled. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by reading SPSR with SPIF set and then accessing SPDR.

fields.name: WCOL
fields.text: Write collision flag: set when SPDR is written during a transfer. Cleared, with SPIF, by reading SPSR with WCOL set and then accessing SPDR.

fields.name: SPI2X
fields.text: Double SPI speed: 1 doubles SCK in master mode, giving a minimum SCK period of two CPU clock periods. As a slave the SPI is guaranteed only at fosc/4 or below. The SPI also serves for downloading and uploading program memory and EEPROM.

fields.name: SPDR

fields.name: RXC0
fields.text: Set while the receive buffer holds unread data; clears once it is empty. Disabling the Receiver flushes the buffer and clears it. Can raise the Receive Complete interrupt.

fields.name: TXC0
fields.text: Set once the whole frame has left the Transmit Shift Register and nothing new waits in UDR0. Cleared when the Transmit Complete interrupt runs, or by writing 1 to it. Can raise the Transmit Complete interrupt.

fields.name: UDRE0
fields.text: 1 when the transmit buffer UDR0 is empty and can take new data. Set after reset, showing the Transmitter is ready. Can raise the Data Register Empty interrupt.

fields.name: FE0
fields.text: Set when the next character in the receive buffer arrived with its first stop bit at 0; 0 when that stop bit was 1. Holds until UDR0 is read. Write 0 here whenever UCSR0A is written.

fields.name: DOR0
fields.text: Set on a Data OverRun: the receive buffer is full with two characters, a further character sits in the Receive Shift Register, and another start bit is seen. Holds until UDR0 is read. Write 0 here whenever UCSR0A is written.

fields.name: UPE0
fields.text: Set when the next character in the receive buffer arrived with a parity error while parity checking was on (UPM01 = 1). Holds until UDR0 is read. Write 0 here whenever UCSR0A is written.

fields.name: U2X0
fields.text: Asynchronous mode only: 1 drops the baud rate divisor from 16 to 8, doubling the rate. Write 0 in synchronous mode.

fields.name: MPCM0
fields.text: Multi-processor Communication mode enable: at 1 the Receiver ignores every incoming frame that carries no address information. The Transmitter is not affected.

fields.text: Division factor of the bit rate generator, the divider that makes the SCL frequency in Master modes.

fields.name: TWINT
fields.text: Goes to 1 once the TWI completes an operation and needs a software response; with the I-bit in SREG and TWIE set, the TWI interrupt vector runs. SCL low is stretched while it is set. Software clears it by writing 1; running the interrupt does not clear it. Clearing it starts the next TWI operation, so finish all access to TWAR, TWSR and TWDR first.

fields.name: TWEA
fields.text: 1 makes the TWI send ACK when its own slave address is received, when a general call arrives with TWGCE in TWAR set, or when a data byte comes in as Master Receiver or Slave Receiver. Writing 0 detaches the device from the bus for a while; writing 1 again restores address recognition.

fields.name: TWSTA
fields.text: Write 1 to become bus Master: the TWI sends a START once the bus is free, waiting for a STOP first if it is busy. Software must clear it after the START has gone out.

fields.name: TWSTO
fields.text: In Master mode, writing 1 sends a STOP on the bus, and the bit clears itself once the STOP is done. In Slave mode, writing 1 sends no STOP but recovers from an error: the TWI returns to unaddressed Slave mode and releases SCL and SDA to high impedance.

fields.name: TWWC

fields.name: TWEN

fields.name: TWIE

fields.name: TWS

registers.name: SPMCSR
registers.title: Store Program Memory Control and Status Register

fields.name: SPMIE
fields.text: 1, with the I-bit in the Status Register set, enables the SPM ready interrupt, which is executed for as long as SPMEN in SPMCSR is 0.

fields.name: RWWSB
fields.text: Hardware sets it when self-programming (Page Erase or Page Write) of the RWW section begins; the RWW section cannot be accessed while it is set. Cleared by writing RWWSRE to 1 after the operation finishes, or on its own when a page load starts.

fields.name: SIGRD
fields.text: Written to 1 together with SPMEN, makes the next LPM within three clock cycles read a signature row byte into the destination register. An SPM within four cycles of setting SIGRD and SPMEN does nothing. Reserved for future use; not to be used.

fields.name: RWWSRE
fields.text: Reopens the RWW section for reading after a Page Erase or Page Write to it. Once programming is over (SPMEN cleared), writing it to 1 with SPMEN makes the next SPM within four clock cycles re-enable the section. It cannot do so while SPMEN shows the Flash busy. Writing it during a Flash load aborts the load and loses the loaded data.

fields.name: BLBSET
fields.text: Written to 1 with SPMEN, makes the next SPM within four clock cycles set the Boot Lock bits from R0; R1 and the Z-pointer address are ignored. Clears itself when the lock bits are set or if no SPM follows within four cycles. An (E)LPM within three cycles of setting BLBSET and SPMEN reads the Lock bits or the Fuse bits, chosen by Z0, into the destination register.

fields.name: PGWRT
fields.text: Written to 1 with SPMEN, makes the next SPM within four clock cycles write the temporary buffer to the page addressed by the high part of the Z-pointer; R1 and R0 are ignored. Clears itself when the write finishes or if no SPM follows within four cycles. The CPU halts for the whole write if the NRWW section is addressed.

fields.name: PGERS
fields.text: Written to 1 with SPMEN, makes the next SPM within four clock cycles erase the page addressed by the high part of the Z-pointer; R1 and R0 are ignored. Clears itself when the erase finishes or if no SPM follows within four cycles. The CPU halts for the whole operation if the NRWW section is addressed.

fields.name: SPMEN
fields.text: Enables SPM for the next four clock cycles. Written with RWWSRE, BLBSET, PGWRT or PGERS, the next SPM does that operation; written alone, the next SPM stores R1:R0 in the temporary page buffer at the Z-pointer address, ignoring the Z-pointer's LSB. Clears itself when the SPM completes or if none comes within four cycles; during Page Erase and Page Write it stays 1 until the operation ends. Lower five bits other than 10001, 01001, 00101, 00011 or 00001 do nothing. Only one SPM may be active at a time.
